newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends lower, retracing from sharp gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends lower, retracing from sharp gains.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended lower on Wednesday on a correction from the week's precipitous gains, pit sources said.
"It was a 'back and fill' day after the rally," a pit source said. "All of this today was profit taking."
Floor sources said the new crop was beginning to be the focal point of the market as old crop supplies dwindled and demand dried up.
Traders had been watching weather developments in key growing regions of Louisiana, Arkansas and Texas. Some areas were reporting soil crusting problems.
"We're keeping an eye on this crop," one pit source said. "We're dealing with an average crop at best and we're hearing about a lot of crusting problems.
Traders noted USDA pegged new crop production at 162.5 million cwt, down five percent from the previous year. That would mark the third straight year of declining production, a trader said.
Rice ended seven to one cent per cwt lower with July off seven at $11.60.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 800 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 818.
